svg.text: Agentic Health Claim Adjudication — Integration Architecture

text.tspan: : End-User → Core → Foundation, dependencies run one way only, top to bottom. | ODC (OutSystems Developer Cloud) + AI Agent Workbench | 17/09/2026
The platform running the whole claim application — owned and developed by BnK
Contains only screens and navigation. No business logic, no direct calls to external systems.
Submit claims · upload documents · track · supplement
Queue · image ↔ figure comparison · approval · agent log
Map the benefit schedule · load group policies
Reusable business concepts. Money is calculated only here.
· 13-step chain computing money per expense line
· Benefit snapshot at the service date, then frozen (P-02)
· Append-only limit ledger: annual · episode · day · co-payment
· Claim state machine and approval authority
Agents read and propose, they do not write money.
AG-0 Orchestrator · AG-1 Intake · AG-2 Cross-check
AG-3 Clinical · AG-4 Catalogue · AG-5 Drafting
Agent tools are CLM_Core Server Actions — they do not call REST externally.
Wraps external systems. Knows nothing about claim business — only translates formats and tolerates errors.
Hackathon: reads the seed in ODC.
Switch to the real system via Site Setting

svg.text: Dependency rules of the Architecture Canvas

text.tspan: : End-User calls Core, Core calls Foundation. No reverse direction, no lateral calls between two modules of the same layer.
This way, replacing an external system means changing only one Layer 3 module, with no ripple upward.

svg.text: EXTERNAL SYSTEMS · REST / JSON over HTTPS

svg.text: The "LOGO" boxes are where the real logos go

text.tspan: The four dashed boxes labelled LOGO keep their exact size so you can drop a logo file into them in draw.io (drag an image onto the box, or Edit Style →
I did not pre-draw logos because they are trademarks of OutSystems, InsureMO and the bank — taking them from each party's official brand kit gives the right version and proportions.
